newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk says Conrail costs reduce quarterly income.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk says Conrail costs reduce quarterly income.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp. said Wednesday that costs related to its proposed takeover of Conrail Inc. reduced its second-quarter earnings by $10.7 million.
The freight railroad said net income totalled $190.1 million, down nearly 5 percent, from $199.5 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share were $1.52, vs. $1.57 a share in the 1996 period.
Norfolk said the acquisition of Conrail trimmed its net income by $10.7 million, or 9 cents a share, and reduced six-month net income by $62.6 million, or 50 cents a share.
Excluding the Conrail impact, second-quarter profits would have totalled a record $200.8 million, or $1.61 a share, for the quarter, in line with Wall Street expectations.

Norfolk Southern and rival CSX Corp. agreed in April to a joint $10.3 billion purchase of Conrail after waging a six-month battle for control of the East Coast railroad. The proposed transaction, which is subject to approval by federal regulators, calls for Norfolk to pay $5.8 billion for a 58 percent share of Conrail.
On Tuesday, CSX Corp. said the Conrail takeover reduced its quarterly earnings by $18 million, or 9 cents a share.
Norfolk said strong growth in the railroad's container and chemicals transportation sectors boosted revenues by nearly 2 percent for the quarter, to $1.3 billion.

Separately, Norfolk Chief Financial Officer Henry Wolf said the Conrail acquisition would be less of a drag on net income in 1998 than had been previously forecast. Conrail-related costs will lower Norfolk's earnings by between 1 and 2 percent in 1998, as opposed to earlier estimates of 3 percent, he said.
Wolf added that the Conrail deal would boost net income by 14 percent in 1999, up from the company's previous estimate of 6 percent.
Norfolk's stock rose $1.56 to a 52-week high of $114.31 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.
